declarations.documentation:
One model step over the conversation + tool schemas — THE provider seam. A provider module serves
this request for the extent of a continuation (`use gemini.provider(...)`), so the loop stays
provider-agnostic and providers stay loop-agnostic. The reply is an OUTCOME sum, never a throw: on
success `inferred(result)` carries the step's decision AND its token accounting (`types.step_result`,
so any loop over this seam can meter its context for free); on failure `inference_failed(error)`
carries the `step_error` the provider gave up on (its retries exhausted, or a fatal status). Handing the
failure back as a VALUE — rather than throwing from the provider's DEEP handler — is what lets each loop
decide at its own PERFORM site whether to absorb the failure (the region loop abandons just that turn and
lives on) or re-raise it into its own caller (the one-shot loops): a deep handler can only throw OUT of
its own context, never INTO the loop's, so the resume value is the only channel that reaches the loop.
declarations.name: infer_step
declarations.signature: request infer_step(history: array[types.message], tool_metas: array[reflection.agent_metadata]) -> step_outcome

declarations.name: step_error
declarations.signature: type step_error = json.parse_error | http.status_error | http.fetch_error | empty_reply

declarations.documentation:
One model step's OUTCOME success: the provider produced a step (`types.step_result` for `infer_step`,
`types.object_result` for `infer_object`). Generic over the payload so both seam requests share one sum shape.
declarations.name: inferred

declarations.documentation:
One model step's OUTCOME failure: the provider gave up — a transient error past its retry budget, or a
fatal status / malformed body. Carried back as a VALUE so a loop handles it at its perform site, rather than
the provider throwing out of its own deep handler and unwinding the whole loop with it.
declarations.name: inference_failed

parameters.documentation: The step error the provider surfaced.
parameters.label: error

error.description: The step error the provider surfaced.

declarations.documentation:
One structured-output step over the conversation — the seam's second request, served by the same
provider handler as `infer_step`. @schema@ is the JSON Schema the reply must conform to (each
provider maps it onto its native constrained decoding); the reply is an OUTCOME — `inferred(result)`
with the decoded object and usage, or `inference_failed(error)`. Prefer `infer_structured[T]`, which
reifies T's schema, validates the reply, and re-raises a failure at your own call site.
declarations.name: infer_object
declarations.signature: request infer_object(history: array[types.message], schema: unknown) -> object_outcome

declarations.checkedType: agent(history: array[call_turn | result_turn | turn]) -> string with infer_step | throw[empty_reply | fetch_error | status_error | parse_error]
declarations.documentation:
Infer a single reply with no tools (the common chat case). A provider failure re-raises here as
`prelude.throw[step_error]` — this is a one-shot call, so a caller that wants to survive a failed step
installs its own handler (the region loop does not use this; it drives the seam directly and absorbs).
declarations.name: reply

declarations.checkedType: agent(history: array[call_turn | result_turn | turn]) -> T1 with infer_object | throw[empty_reply | fetch_error | status_error | parse_error | validation_error]
declarations.documentation:
Infer a single reply as a typed value — structured output with the type as the contract:
`reflection.schema_of[T]` reifies T's schema, the ambient provider decodes against it natively
(Gemini's responseSchema, OpenAI's response_format, Anthropic a forced tool), and the decoded object
validates as T (`json.validate` — a nonconforming reply throws `json.validation_error`). Instantiate
T explicitly; it appears only in the result, so it is never inferable. An object type
(`type shape = { ... }`) makes the friendliest model-facing schema — a data type asks the model to
produce its `$katari_constructor` wrapper too.
declarations.name: infer_structured

declarations.documentation:
The provider's API finished a step WITHOUT an answer: no tool call and no reply text, with a
finish reason other than a normal stop (an output-token truncation that ate the whole answer, a
safety block). Deliberately distinct from a NORMAL empty reply (finish reason STOP), which stays a
legitimate quiet `step_final("")` — the region loop's monitors depend on it. Not transient: the
same context replays into the same truncation, so it surfaces to the app instead of burning retries.
declarations.name: empty_reply

declarations.checkedType: agent(error: empty_reply | fetch_error | status_error | parse_error) -> boolean
declarations.documentation:
Whether a step error is TRANSIENT — worth a backoff and a retry — as opposed to fatal. A transport
failure (`http.fetch_error`: DNS, a refused connection, a timeout, a mid-flight restart) is always
transient; a status error is transient for 408 (request timeout), 429 (rate limit) and any 5xx
(server-side), and fatal for every other status (401/403/404 … — a retry will not fix them); a
`json.parse_error` is fatal (a malformed body will not parse on a retry).
declarations.name: is_transient

declarations.documentation:
The backoff delay in milliseconds before retry @attempt@ (0-based): @base_ms@ doubled per attempt (base,
2×base, 4×base, …) and capped at one minute, so a long outage does not sleep unboundedly between the final
tries.
declarations.name: backoff_ms
declarations.signature: agent backoff_ms(attempt: integer, base_ms: number) -> number

declarations.documentation:
The outcome of ONE provider step attempt, threaded back to a provider's retry loop: the step's @result@
on success. A provider's per-attempt helper catches a `step_error` into `attempt_err` so the loop can
classify it (`is_transient`) and either back off and retry or propagate.
declarations.name: attempt_ok

declarations.documentation: The outcome of ONE provider step attempt: the @error@ the attempt caught, for the retry loop to classify.
declarations.name: attempt_err

declarations.documentation:
Two tools in one loop's tool list share a metadata name, so the model's pick could not be routed
unambiguously (dispatch matches by name — the first match would silently win, and the other tool
would be unreachable). A configuration defect the app fixes — a `prefix` on one of the colliding MCP
connections, or a rename — typed so a supervisor reports it instead of the run panicking.
declarations.name: duplicate_tool

declarations.documentation:
Validate one step's assembled tool metadata: every name unique, or the typed `duplicate_tool`.
Every loop runs its tool list through this once per turn, so a colliding list fails loudly at the
first step instead of silently routing every pick to whichever tool sorts first.
declarations.name: ensure_unique_names

declarations.documentation:
Tool: load an image file into your visual context. Pass the file's handle object — a bare
{"$katari_ref": "<id>"} suffices (copy the id from the conversation); the image content arrives with
this tool's result, so you can see it on your next step.
declarations.name: view_image

declarations.checkedType: agent(history: array[call_turn | result_turn | turn], max_steps: integer, tool_budget_milliseconds?: number, tools: array[agent(...never) -> unknown with throw[unknown] | {...E4 lacks race_settled}]) -> string with infer_step | throw[duplicate_tool | empty_reply | fetch_error | status_error | parse_error] | {...E4 lacks race_settled} | io
declarations.documentation:
Run the tool-using model loop, generic over the tools' shared effect @E@: derive each tool's schema
with `reflection.get_metadata`, then up to @max_steps@ times perform `infer_step` against the ambient
provider; on a batch of tool calls, dispatch them all CONCURRENTLY with `parallel for` (each resolves
its tool by name and invokes it by value via `reflection.call_agent`, validating the model's args
against the tool's schema), then feed every result back as a new turn; on a final answer, return it.
declarations.name: infer_with_tools

parameters.documentation: The per-tool-call budget in milliseconds, or `null` (the default) for no deadline — see `take_turn`.
parameters.label: tool_budget_milliseconds

declarations.signature: agent infer_with_tools[effect E](history: array[types.message], tools: array[agent never -> unknown with {...E, prelude.throw[unknown]}], max_steps: integer, tool_budget_milliseconds: number | null ?= null) -> string

declarations.documentation:
WHO a step is on behalf of: the @author@ of the NEWEST user turn in @history@ — taken AS-IS, null
included, with no further scanning back. The newest user turn is the turn that triggered the current
model turn, so a system-triggered turn (a monitor tick, whose injection carries `author = null`)
shields the earlier human turns instead of misattributing the step to whoever spoke last; the
loop-synthesized user turns (the budget close, the empty-final renudge) are also null and likewise
read as unattributed. Providers lift a non-null result into their end-user metadata field
(Anthropic's `metadata.user_id`, OpenAI's `safety_identifier`); Gemini has no such field and ignores
it.
declarations.name: attribution

declarations.documentation:
The one-shot renudge a loop plays when the model's final step came back EMPTY: an empty string is
a lost answer in an interactive exchange (a thinking model can finish a heavy turn with only thought
parts and no text), so the loop asks ONCE for a plain-text answer before accepting the silence. The
wording also names the legitimate way out — a watcher protocol with truly nothing to report answers
empty again, and the second empty is accepted as-is.
declarations.name: empty_reply_nudge

declarations.documentation:
The forced tool-less close every loop plays when its step budget runs out: a user turn telling the
model the budget is spent, so ONE last step commits to an answer from what the tools already gathered
instead of discarding it.
declarations.name: budget_exhausted_turn

declarations.checkedType: agent(budget_milliseconds: null | number, call: tool_call, tools: array[agent(...never) -> unknown with throw[unknown] | {...E5 lacks race_settled}]) -> tool_result with {...E5 lacks throw | race_settled} | io
declarations.documentation:
Find the tool whose metadata name is the model's pick and invoke it by value via
`reflection.call_agent` (the model's args ride as a plain value, and the delegation boundary
validates them against the tool's schema — the compiled signature of a Katari agent, or the
server-declared schema of an MCP tool — while the boundary's unconditional wire→value conversion turns
any replayed `$katari_ref` into the `file` it denotes). Every way a call can go wrong is fed back to the
model as an error result it reads and corrects on its next step: a hallucinated name (nothing matches), a
tool that panics, a tool's own typed `throw`, malformed args (a `reflection.call_error` from the
boundary), and a call that outruns @budget_milliseconds@ (raced via `time.with_deadline`, the late
call cancelled) alike — none of them reaches the app root. The result's `file` values are collected off the
result tree so the provider can show them to the model (their `$katari_ref` handles are already visible in
the result text).
declarations.name: dispatch_one

parameters.documentation: The per-call budget in milliseconds, or `null` for no deadline.
parameters.label: budget_milliseconds

declarations.signature: agent dispatch_one[effect E](tools: array[agent never -> unknown with {...E, prelude.throw[unknown]}], call: types.tool_call, budget_milliseconds: number | null) -> types.tool_result

declarations.documentation:
Collect every `file` value out of a tool result's value tree: `reflection.call_agent` returns the
tool's result as a plain value, so a `file` the tool produced (a generated image, an MCP tool's
screenshot) is an actual `file` leaf — found wherever it sits (a bare return, the MCP bridge's
{ text, files } record, or nested structure).
declarations.name: collect_result_files
declarations.signature: agent collect_result_files(node: unknown) -> array[file] with pure

declarations.documentation:
How a session compacts its context once it outgrows the threshold. @threshold_tokens@ compares
against the freshest step's measured occupancy (`usage.input_tokens + output_tokens`); @prompt@
frames the summarization step; @keep_recent@ is how many trailing history elements survive
verbatim — extended forward to a clean `turn` boundary, so a call turn is never severed from the
results that answer it.
declarations.name: compaction
declarations.signature: data compaction(threshold_tokens: integer, prompt: string, keep_recent: integer)

declarations.documentation:
The default compaction policy both session shapes fall back to: compact past 100k tokens,
summarize under the standard self-note prompt, keep the last 8 history elements verbatim.
declarations.name: default_compaction

declarations.documentation: The verdict on a measured context occupancy: still under the threshold, with the room left.
declarations.name: within_budget

parameters.documentation: Tokens still free under the threshold.
parameters.label: remaining

remaining.description: Tokens still free under the threshold.

declarations.documentation: The verdict on a measured context occupancy: over the threshold — time to compact.
declarations.name: over_budget

parameters.documentation: The measured occupancy that tripped the threshold.
parameters.label: used

used.description: The measured occupancy that tripped the threshold.

declarations.documentation:
Classify a measured context occupancy against the policy threshold — the compaction machinery's
one numeric comparison; everything downstream dispatches on the returned sum.
declarations.name: classify_budget
declarations.signature: agent classify_budget(used: integer, policy: compaction) -> budget

declarations.documentation:
The integer at a provider's usage field, or 0 when the field is absent — a provider that omits a
count still yields a usable measurement. Providers read their wire usage through this.
declarations.name: token_count

declarations.checkedType: agent(history: array[call_turn | result_turn | turn], start: integer) -> integer
declarations.documentation:
The first index at or after @start@ whose element is a plain `turn` — the clean cut for `compact`:
a `call_turn` must never be severed from the `result_turn` that answers it (a provider replays them
as a matched pair), so the kept tail always starts on a turn. No turn after @start@ means nothing
safely survives, and the whole history summarizes.
declarations.name: turn_boundary
declarations.signature: agent turn_boundary(history: array[types.message], start: integer) -> integer

declarations.documentation:
A history element as summarizer-input text: turns as role-prefixed lines, tool traffic as compact
notes — enough for the summary to preserve what happened, nothing wire-shaped.
declarations.name: render_message

declarations.checkedType: agent(history: array[call_turn | result_turn | turn], policy: compaction) -> array[call_turn | result_turn | turn] with infer_step
declarations.documentation:
Compress a conversation to fit its budget again: everything before the kept tail (the last
@policy.keep_recent@ elements, extended to a clean turn boundary) is summarized by one tool-less
model step under @policy.prompt@, and the summary replaces it as a single opening turn. A history
that is all tail comes back unchanged. Exported on its own so a hand-rolled loop can compact too —
`serve_session` is this plus the metering that decides when.
declarations.name: compact
declarations.signature: agent compact(history: array[types.message], policy: compaction) -> array[types.message]

declarations.documentation:
Raised once per incoming message of a served session; `serve_session`'s handler answers it with
the model's reply. The app's transport bridge performs it — fold any routing detail (a channel id, a
thread ts) into @content@ on the way in, route the returned reply on the way out.
declarations.name: session_message

parameters.documentation: The incoming message, routing details folded in.
parameters.label: content

content.description: The incoming message, routing details folded in.

declarations.signature: request session_message(content: string, files: array[file]) -> string

declarations.documentation:
A served session's durable state: the running conversation and the freshest measured context
occupancy — 0 until a step has run, and again right after a compaction until the next step
re-measures.
declarations.name: session_state

declarations.documentation: One served turn's outcome: the reply, the advanced conversation, and the freshest measurement.
declarations.name: session_turn
declarations.signature: data session_turn(reply: string, conversation: array[types.message], used_tokens: integer)

declarations.documentation:
A turn the provider FAILED mid-way: the conversation as far as it got (completed call / result
exchanges included) and the step error. `take_turn` hands failure back as a VALUE so a long-lived
caller — an app-owned event loop — can ABSORB it as one match arm (annotate the conversation, notify
a channel, await the next event) instead of unwinding; a one-shot caller re-raises it
(`infer_with_tools`, `serve_session`).
declarations.name: failed_turn

declarations.checkedType: agent(history: array[call_turn | result_turn | turn]) -> (failed_turn | session_turn) with infer_step
declarations.documentation:
ONE tool-less step over @history@, folded to a `turn_result`: the shared closing move of the
budget exhaustion and the empty-final renudge — both must commit to an answer without tools, and
both hand a provider failure back as a value.
declarations.name: closing_step

declarations.checkedType: agent(conversation: array[call_turn | result_turn | turn], max_steps: integer, nudge_empty_reply?: boolean, tool_budget_milliseconds?: number, tools: array[agent(...never) -> unknown with throw[unknown] | {...E6 lacks race_settled}]) -> (failed_turn | session_turn) with infer_step | throw[duplicate_tool] | {...E6 lacks race_settled} | io
declarations.documentation:
THE turn loop — advance @conversation@ by one model turn and hand back a VALUE either way: up to
@max_steps@ steps against the ambient provider, tool batches dispatched in parallel, the model's
reply appended as a model turn, and the LAST step's `input + output` carried out as the context
measurement (each step's input covers the whole context, so only the freshest figure is the
occupancy — steps do not add). Budget spent, one forced tool-less close commits to an answer; an
EMPTY final is renudged once for a plain-text answer (an empty here is a lost answer, not a signal —
a caller whose protocol gives the empty reply meaning still receives the second empty as-is). A
provider failure at any step returns `failed_turn` rather than unwinding, so an app-owned event loop
absorbs it as one match arm. This is the ai package's ONE loop: sessions (`serve_session`) and
resident agents (an app-owned `observation` handler over a `region` nursery) are compositions over
it. The two knobs are policy the caller owns: @tool_budget_milliseconds@ deadlines every tool call
(null = no deadline), and @nudge_empty_reply@ = false accepts an empty final as-is — for a caller
whose protocol gives the empty reply meaning (a watcher that stays quiet), so a quiet turn does not
pay the renudge's extra step.
declarations.name: take_turn

parameters.documentation:
The per-tool-call budget in milliseconds — every call races it via `time.with_deadline`, and a timeout
comes back to the model as an error result. `null` (the default) sets no deadline.
parameters.label: tool_budget_milliseconds

parameters.documentation:
Whether an empty final reply is renudged once for a plain-text answer (the interactive default).
Pass `false` when the empty reply is a meaningful signal in your protocol.
parameters.label: nudge_empty_reply

declarations.signature: agent take_turn[effect E](conversation: array[types.message], tools: array[agent never -> unknown with {...E, prelude.throw[unknown]}], max_steps: integer, tool_budget_milliseconds: number | null ?= null, nudge_empty_reply: boolean ?= true) -> turn_result

declarations.checkedType: agent(context: array[call_turn | result_turn | turn], continuation: agent(value: null) -> T7 with session_message | {...E8 lacks race_settled}, max_steps: integer, policy?: compaction, tool_budget_milliseconds?: number, tools: array[agent(...never) -> unknown with throw[unknown] | {...E8 lacks race_settled}]) -> T7 with infer_step | throw[duplicate_tool | empty_reply | fetch_error | status_error | parse_error] | {...E8 lacks race_settled} | io
declarations.documentation:
Serve a chat session for the extent of @continuation@ — the hand-rolled serve skeleton as one
provider, with token metering and automatic compaction. The handler's var carries the conversation
across messages (durable by construction: it survives a runtime restart like any run state); each
`session_message` runs one tool loop and answers with the reply. After each turn the freshest
measured occupancy is classified against @threshold_tokens@: over it, the conversation compacts
(`compact`) under @compact_prompt@, keeping the last @keep_recent@ elements verbatim. The ambient
provider (`use gemini.provider(...)` …) and any @E@ handlers are installed by the caller, exactly as
for `infer_with_tools`; the continuation bridges its transport into `session_message` and typically
never returns (a `watch_messages` loop).
declarations.name: serve_session

parameters.documentation:
The conversation the model starts from (PRIOR TURNS only — standing instructions belong in the
provider's `system` parameter, which every provider takes and compaction never touches; anything put
here is history, and the first compaction folds it into the summary).
parameters.label: context

parameters.documentation: The tools of every turn's loop.
parameters.label: tools

parameters.documentation: The compaction policy — one `compaction(...)` datum; `null` (the default) is `default_compaction`.
parameters.label: policy

parameters.documentation: The per-tool-call budget in milliseconds, or `null` (the default) for no deadline — see `take_turn`.
parameters.label: tool_budget_milliseconds

parameters.documentation: The session body: bridges a transport into `session_message`.
parameters.label: continuation

declarations.signature: agent serve_session[R, effect E](context: array[types.message], tools: array[agent never -> unknown with {...E, prelude.throw[unknown]}], max_steps: integer, policy: compaction | null ?= null, tool_budget_milliseconds: number | null ?= null, continuation: agent(value: null) -> R with {...E, session_message}) -> R

declarations.documentation:
THE event→model channel: a background fiber (an always-on source such as a chat watcher, or a
started watch) pushes @content@ (plus any @files@) from @source@ into the model's context.
FIRE-AND-FORGET (`-> null`): a fiber only reports — the app's serving handler injects the report as
a user turn, advances the conversation (`take_turn`), and routes the reply wherever it belongs.
@files@ ride the injection turn's `files` slot — the same text + files split as `types.turn` — so
the provider's existing inline policy shows the model any attached image. @author@ rides the
injection turn's `author`, so the triggered turn's requests carry the right abuse-attribution
metadata (`ai.attribution`).
declarations.name: observation

parameters.documentation: Which fiber is reporting (e.g. "discord:<channel>"); it labels the report's injection turn.
parameters.label: source

parameters.documentation: The report to inject into the model's context.
parameters.label: content

parameters.documentation: Any files attached to the report (a Discord / Slack attachment), injected on the report's turn so the provider inlines them for the model; defaults to none.
parameters.label: files

parameters.documentation: The opaque end-user tag of the human behind this report (e.g. a hashed chat-user id), or `null` for a system report (a scheduled tick).
parameters.label: author

author.description: The opaque end-user tag of the human behind this report (e.g. a hashed chat-user id), or `null` for a system report (a scheduled tick).

content.description: The report to inject into the model's context.

files.description: Any files attached to the report (a Discord / Slack attachment), injected on the report's turn so the provider inlines them for the model; defaults to none.

source.description: Which fiber is reporting (e.g. "discord:<channel>"); it labels the report's injection turn.

declarations.signature: request observation(source: string, content: string, files: array[file] ?= [], author: string | null ?= null) -> null

declarations.checkedType: agent(prompt: agent(value: null) -> string with E9, schedule: cron | interval, source: string) -> never with observation | E9 | io
declarations.documentation:
A watch body reduced to its essence: on every occurrence of @schedule@, inject the freshly
computed @prompt@ into the model's context as an observation from @source@ — the scheduled
self-prompt every periodic watcher (check a repo, track a topic, look at a calendar) hand-rolled as
its own `time.watch` adapter. @prompt@ is an agent so each tick recomputes it (an env-configured
target re-reads, a date renders current); its effects @E@ flow to the app's handlers. Never returns:
fork it into the app's nursery and cancel its fiber to stop.
declarations.name: watch_prompt

parameters.documentation: Which watcher is reporting; labels the injection turn (e.g. "repo-issues").
parameters.label: source

parameters.documentation: Computes the report to inject, fresh at every occurrence.
parameters.label: prompt

declarations.signature: agent watch_prompt[effect E](source: string, prompt: agent(value: null) -> string with E, schedule: time.schedule) -> never with {...E, observation} | io

declarations.checkedType: agent(continuation: agent(value: null) -> T10 with observation | {...E11 lacks race_settled}, deliver_to: agent(reply: string) -> null with {...E11 lacks race_settled}, max_steps: integer, policy?: compaction, tool_budget_milliseconds?: number, tools: array[agent(...never) -> unknown with throw[unknown] | {...E11 lacks race_settled}]) -> T10 with infer_step | throw[duplicate_tool] | {...E11 lacks race_settled} | io
declarations.documentation:
Serve a RESIDENT agent's observations for the extent of @continuation@ — the resident sibling of
`serve_session`, and the one home of the absorb / deliver / compact skeleton every resident app
hand-rolled: each `observation` injects as a user turn (source-labelled, files and author riding it),
one `take_turn` advances the conversation, and the reply leaves through @deliver_to@. THE RESIDENT
PROTOCOL IS BUILT IN: an empty (blank) reply means 'nothing to say' — it is not delivered and not
renudged, so a quiet watcher tick costs exactly one model step. A provider failure is ABSORBED as one
match arm — @deliver_to@ gets a one-line notice, the conversation is annotated, and the loop awaits
the next event — because a resident must outlive a failed step. After each turn the measured
occupancy classifies against @policy@ and an over-budget conversation compacts. The conversation
starts EMPTY: standing instructions belong in the provider's `system` parameter, which compaction
never touches. Install this INSIDE your providers and ABOVE your `region.watch` call; the region
wiring — the nursery, its ceiling, the registry, the forks — stays yours.
declarations.name: serve_observations

parameters.documentation: The tools of every turn's loop.
parameters.label: tools

parameters.documentation: Where a turn's non-empty reply (and a step-failure notice) is delivered.
parameters.label: deliver_to

parameters.documentation: The compaction policy — one `compaction(...)` datum; `null` (the default) is `default_compaction`.
parameters.label: policy

parameters.documentation: The per-tool-call budget in milliseconds, or `null` (the default) for no deadline — see `take_turn`.
parameters.label: tool_budget_milliseconds

parameters.documentation: The resident body: forks its sources and typically never returns (`region.watch`).
parameters.label: continuation

declarations.signature: agent serve_observations[R, effect E](tools: array[agent never -> unknown with {...E, prelude.throw[unknown]}], max_steps: integer, deliver_to: agent(reply: string) -> null with E, policy: compaction | null ?= null, tool_budget_milliseconds: number | null ?= null, continuation: agent(value: null) -> R with {...E, observation}) -> R

declarations.checkedType: agent(continuation: agent(value: null) -> T12 with infer_step | E13, inject: agent(value: null) -> string with infer_step | E13) -> T12 with infer_step | E13
declarations.documentation:
Middleware over the seam: EVERY `infer_step`, prepend @inject@'s freshly computed text as a user
turn and re-perform outward to the ambient provider — the generalization of the bot-side pattern
that re-injects the current time and a memory index each turn. Install it INSIDE the provider
(`use gemini.provider(...)` then `use ai.with_context(inject = ...)`), so the re-performed step
reaches the model. An EMPTY injection skips the extra turn; the injected turn is never part of the
conversation a loop persists (it is derived fresh each step, so persisting it would double it).
`infer_object` passes through un-injected — structured extraction states its own context.
declarations.name: with_context

parameters.documentation: Computes the note to prepend this step — ambient state (the time, a memory index), fresh each step.
parameters.label: inject

parameters.documentation: The program to run with the injection installed.
parameters.label: continuation

declarations.signature: agent with_context[R, effect E](inject: agent(value: null) -> string with {...E, infer_step}, continuation: agent(value: null) -> R with {...E, infer_step}) -> R with E | infer_step

declarations.documentation:
A deterministic two-way mapping between a tool's real (qualified) name and the shortened name a
provider sends on the wire. @real_to_wire@ is keyed by the qualified name (used when encoding a tool
declaration or replaying a call turn), @wire_to_real@ by the wire name (used to reverse the model's
pick); both are total over one step's tools — see @build_name_map@.
declarations.name: name_map

declarations.documentation:
Fold a wire name onto a qualified name: every character outside a provider's `[a-zA-Z0-9_-]` name
alphabet (the dot of a qualified name, above all) folds to `_`, then the result is capped at the
providers' 64-character limit.
declarations.name: sanitize_name

declarations.documentation:
Disambiguate a colliding wire name with an ordinal suffix (`_2`, `_3`, …), reserving room so the
result still fits the 64-character cap.
declarations.name: suffixed_name
declarations.signature: agent suffixed_name(base: string, index: integer) -> string

declarations.documentation:
Choose a free wire name for @real@ given the wire names already @taken@: its sanitized form, or —
when sanitizing collapsed two distinct qualified names onto one token, or truncation shared a prefix —
the first free ordinal-suffixed form. The suffix is decided by @taken@'s size (processing order), so
the choice is deterministic.
declarations.name: assign_wire_name

parameters.documentation: The wire names already assigned this step.
parameters.label: taken

taken.description: The wire names already assigned this step.

declarations.signature: agent assign_wire_name(taken: record[string], real: string) -> string

declarations.documentation:
Build the deterministic wire-name @name_map@ for one step's tools. Walking @tool_metas@ in order,
each tool's qualified name is assigned a free wire name against the names already placed, so the same
tool list always yields the same map — which is why the map needs no durable state (see the section
note). A provider whose wire vocabulary admits the qualified name (Gemini) never calls this.
declarations.name: build_name_map

declarations.documentation:
The wire name for a qualified tool name — used to encode a tool declaration and to re-encode a
replayed call turn. Falls back to the qualified name for a tool absent from the map (never happens for
a map built from the same step's tools).
declarations.name: wire_name_of
declarations.signature: agent wire_name_of(map: name_map, real: string) -> string

declarations.documentation:
The qualified tool name for a wire name — used to reverse the model's pick so the loop dispatches by
the real name. Falls back to the wire name itself for an unknown name (a hallucinated tool), which the
loop then reports as an unknown tool.
declarations.name: real_name_of

parameters.documentation: The wire name the model returned.
parameters.label: wire

wire.description: The wire name the model returned.

Serve `ai.infer_step` over Anthropic for the extent of the continuation:

thrown — but a TRANSIENT one (a 429 rate limit, a 5xx, a dropped connection) is first retried with
exponential backoff (up to @retry_attempts@ attempts from @retry_base_ms@); only a fatal error or an
exhausted budget surfaces, as a value the loop handles at its own perform site rather than a throw.

declarations.documentation:
The file's recorded content type, or "" when the handle is gone (freed, or never named a live blob).
A gone file cannot inline — its handle note still rides — so `gone` folds to the same "not an image"
signal as an unrecorded type, and never fails a whole step over one stale attachment.
declarations.name: anthropic_content_type

declarations.documentation:
Whether a file inlines as an Anthropic image block: its recorded content type begins "image/" (the
Messages API image block takes only image media types). A file with another or no recorded type stays
a handle note.
declarations.name: anthropic_is_image

declarations.documentation: A text content block — `{ "type": "text", "text": @text@ }`, built as a raw value tree.
declarations.name: anthropic_text_block

declarations.documentation:
An image content block: a base64 `source` whose `media_type` is the file's recorded type and whose
`data` slot holds the file VALUE placed DIRECTLY into the tree. `http.json` materialises that slot —
reading the bytes and base64-ing them in place — only at the send boundary, so the image content never
rides the value plane, the durable call record or the trace.
declarations.name: anthropic_image_block

declarations.documentation:
A turn's content: the plain string (text + every file's handle note) when the turn carries no image,
or an array of one text block plus one image block per image file when it does. An image file inlines
so the model can SEE it; a non-image file stays a handle note (the image block takes only images). The
text block still carries every file's handle note, so the model can replay any of them into a tool.

declarations.documentation:
The step's token accounting off the response's `usage`: prompt tokens are the whole context the
step read, completion tokens what the model generated (an absent field reads as 0).
declarations.name: openai_usage

declarations.checkedType: agent(client: connection, history: array[call_turn | result_turn | turn], tool_metas: array[agent_metadata]) -> step_result with throw[missing_secret | fetch_error | status_error | parse_error | server_error] | io
declarations.documentation:
One OpenAI model step over the history + tool schemas (the body built as a value tree and the reply
parsed by `post_json`, in Katari; only the POST leaves the runtime).
declarations.name: openai_infer_step
declarations.signature: agent openai_infer_step(client: connection, history: array[types.message], tool_metas: array[reflection.agent_metadata]) -> types.step_result

declarations.checkedType: agent(client: connection, history: array[call_turn | result_turn | turn], schema: unknown) -> object_result with throw[missing_secret | fetch_error | status_error | parse_error | server_error] | io
declarations.documentation:
One OpenAI structured-output step: the tool-less message list plus `response_format` pinning the
reply to JSON conforming to @schema@. The name map is empty — a replayed call turn in @history@
rides under its real name via the fallback, fine for the rare structured step over a tool
transcript. The reply content parses back to the decoded object; a non-JSON reply throws
`json.parse_error` (∈ `ai.step_error`).
declarations.name: openai_infer_object
declarations.signature: agent openai_infer_object(client: connection, history: array[types.message], schema: unknown) -> types.object_result

declarations.documentation:
One turn in a conversation: who spoke ("user" / "model"), what they said, and any files attached
to it (a Discord attachment, a generated image). Files ride as blob handles; each provider decides
when to inline their content for the model (see the providers' inline policy). @author@ is the
OPTIONAL opaque end-user tag of a user turn (e.g. a hashed chat-user id) — never shown to the model;
providers lift the newest user turn's author into their abuse-attribution request metadata
(`ai.attribution`). `null` (the default) means the turn is not attributable to an end user: a system
framing turn, a monitor notification, a loop-synthesized turn.
declarations.name: turn
declarations.signature: data turn(role: string, text: string, files: array[file] ?= [], author: string | null ?= null)

declarations.documentation:
One tool the model wants to invoke this step — @name@ is its function name (the dispatch key and
the model-facing call/response record), @opaque@ is any provider token that must be replayed
verbatim on the call turn (Gemini's thought signature, OpenAI's call id), @args@ is the model's
argument object as a parsed value (replayed verbatim into the call turn, and dispatched straight
through `reflection.call_agent`, whose delegation boundary unconditionally turns any `$katari_ref` the
model replayed into the `file` it denotes).
declarations.name: tool_call
declarations.signature: data tool_call(name: string, opaque: string, args: unknown)

declarations.documentation:
A tool's output for the model, keyed by the tool @name@ / @call_id@ so it round-trips as a function
response. @files@ are the `file` values found in the result (a screenshot an MCP tool returned, an
edited image): @text@ already shows their `$katari_ref` handles (the result's wire form), and the provider
additionally inlines their content for the model while the result is fresh.
declarations.name: tool_result
declarations.signature: data tool_result(name: string, call_id: string, text: string, files: array[file])

declarations.documentation: A conversation turn recording the model's tool-call batch — replayed so the next step shows the model what it already asked for.
declarations.name: call_turn

declarations.documentation: A conversation turn carrying the results of a tool-call batch.
declarations.name: result_turn

declarations.documentation: One inference step's decision: a final reply text for the user.
declarations.name: step_final

declarations.documentation: One inference step's decision: invoke a batch of tools (dispatched in parallel, results fed back together).
declarations.name: step_call

declarations.documentation:
One step's token accounting, as the provider's API reported it. @input_tokens@ counts the whole
context the step consumed (every provider re-reads the full history each step), so the FRESHEST
step's figure IS the session's current context occupancy — figures across steps do not add.
@output_tokens@ counts what the model generated on the step.
declarations.name: usage

declarations.documentation: What a provider returns for one model step: the decision plus its token accounting.
declarations.name: step_result

declarations.documentation:
What a provider returns for one structured-output step: the decoded object (the wire's best effort
at the requested schema — `ai.infer_structured` validates it as T) plus the step's token accounting.
declarations.name: object_result
